newsitem.title: USA: Clinton meets Chinese defense minister.
newsitem.headline: Clinton meets Chinese defense minister.

text.p: President Bill Clinton met briefly with Chinese Defence Minister Chi Haotian on Monday, reflecting a thaw in Sino-American relations that began at a meeting in Manila last month.

Clinton met Chi, who played a key role in crushing the 1989 pro-democracy demonstrations in Beijing's Tiananmen Square, as the Chinese official started a round of talks designed to mend fences between Washington and Beijing.

A White House spokeswoman characterised the meeting as primarily a courtesy call. But Clinton press secretary Mike McCurry said beforehand that Clinton and Chi would talk about "the broad nature of the relationship which has been moving in a positive direction."

U.S. relations with China went into a long downward spiral after the Tiananmen crackdown, but Clinton and Chinese President Jiang Zemin agreed at a Nov. 17 Manila meeting to end the official estrangement between their two countries.

McCurry told reporters last Friday that the United States did not consider the Tiananmen issue "irrelevant," but said Chi's visit was important because of the need to maintain peace and stability in Asia.
